BiblicalUsage: The word is the outspread wings of the covering cherub, and it appears once, in the lament over the king of Tyre: thou art the anointed cherub that covereth, with wings spread wide over the holy mountain of God.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the wings tell the story: the cherub was set to cover and guard, and the fall came when the guardian wanted the throne for himself.
